event_name: CIP - ACC/JED - E Cesar Chavez St 400-500 blks - Austin Convention Center Redevelopment
description:
Temporary use of Right of Way Permit has been issued for this location. 
 Details: Demolition and rebuild of the Austin Convention Center

JE Dunn Construction will be performing full demolition and removal of the existing Convention Center, excavate a 45' deep hole in the 6-city block footprint. Erect a new concrete and steel structure and build out the new convention center. Installation of all related new utilities. The project will be occupying 3 lanes on Trinity St., 2 Lanes on Red River. , 4th St pedestrian plaza and one west bound lane on Cesar Chavez and all surrounding sidewalks. The work will be occurring from 4/1/25 - 12/31/28, with deliveries and hauling that will occur 24 hrs. a day with approximately 100 to 1000 trucks a day through the permit duration. 

Haul Schedule:
LATE APRIL '25 TO JULY '25 = 80 - 110 TOTAL TRUCKS PER DAY
SEPT. '25 TO SEPT. '26 = 400 - 570 TOTAL TRUCKS PER DAY
SEPT. '26 TO APRIL '27 = 100 TOTAL TRUCKS PER DAY
APRIL '27 TO DEC. '28 = 30-50 TOTAL TRUCKS PER DAY

*Active work area dimensions 
Trinity - 48' x 1016'
4th St - 63' x 642'
Red River - 41' x 701'
Cesar Chavez - 22' x 436'

event_name: Enertech - Chicon St 1800 BLK - Moonlight Tower Reinstallation
description:
Temporary use of Right of Way Permit has been issued for this location. 
 Details: Work for Moonlight Tower Reinstallation: Two cranes will be set up at the two adjacent sides of the tower. Each crane requires approximately 30 ft of width which requires the closure of Chicon and the partial closure of MLK. The tower section will be transported on a semi-trailer and lowered or lifted by crane to the tower location. Additionally, guy wires will be removed and replaced over the intersection and along the streets in all directions.
The work will be completed during 2 consecutive work days over a weekend. Project impacts: Martin Luther King Blvd (Two Lanes, 1600-2114 blk) and Chicon St (Full Road, 1800-1817blk), one (unpaid) 2 hour parking lane, 2 bike lanes. Sidewalk on east side of Chicon closed from Martin Luther King Blvd to Alley before E 18th St.

Excavation Permit has been issued for this location. 
 Details: *** Original work dates Sep 11, 2026 - Oct 11, 2026 Extended on Sep 25, 2026***WO 707058 ¿ 16th Street Duct Bank - Rio Grande St to Colorado St ¿ AE/Mastec/Primoris - The objective of this project is to provide an accessible and maintainable duct bank system that Austin Energy will use to provide distribution power to the downtown grid. This is a critical segment to connect the new Rainey Street Substation to the downtown power grid, as rapid growth has proven difficult for the existing Brackenridge Substation. The project comprises installing a 9x5¿ duct bank in two sections ¿ a bore section of approximately 224 feet, located approximately 30 feet below 16th Street and an open cut section of approximately 570 feet, approximately 8 feet below 16th Street. This scope also includes small sections of water and wastewater line relocations conflicting with the proposed duct bank. There are temporary erosion control measures and trail re-routes, as well as extensive pavement, including sidewalk, and environmental restoration plans. TCP26-202785 

All of the water and wastewater will be separate trenches except for the two sections that are 20' in sheet 6 and 7. The duct bank will be excavated under the waterline once replaced.

The waterline and wastewater work will be worked separately from the duct bank work.

event_name: CIP/IDIQ - TPW/API - MESA DR 7300-8000 BLK - MILL & OVERLAY
description:
Excavation Permit has been issued for this location. 
 Details: *** Manual Extension End date Oct 31, 2026****** Manual Extension End date Sep 30, 2026***This project is included in the City of Austin Transportation and Public Works 2025 Miscellaneous Streets Overlay IDIQ CLMC1070.  The Work generally consists of providing the following services, including but not limited to all necessary street preparation work as listed, including milling; crack sealing; tack coat; HMAC surface replacement areas and HMAC level up, followed by the installation of an asphalt overlay; lane and pavement markings and traffic control; and adjustment of manholes and water valve boxes. Project locations are throughout the City of Austin.  The operation will mill and pave 1.5 to 2.5 inches of the existing pavement.  We will not adjust pavement grade, add capacity, or change any roadway geometric features.  Pavement markings will be replaced as exist currently.  There are no plans associated with this maintenance work.
